cards.explanation: David and his men march behind the Philistine leaders, right there in the back with Achish. The text says so plainly (1 Samuel 29:2). Achish, king of Gath, is the one walking with them (1 Samuel 27:2). Friends, I think that spot in line is exactly why the commanders start squinting at them.

The answer is True, and Achish is not shy about it. He says David has been with him all these days, even years, and "…from the day he defected until today I have found no fault in him." (1 Samuel 29:3) That's a glowing review from a king, friends. As far as Achish is concerned, David's work history with him is spotless.

The commanders tell Achish to send David back to the place he assigned him. Their words are, "Send that man back and let him return to the place you assigned him." (1 Samuel 29:4) They want David out of the battle line, and they say it plain, friends. No committee, no vote, just a straight order to send him back.

The word is adversary. The commanders say David "…must not go down with us into battle only to become our adversary during the war." (1 Samuel 29:4) An adversary is an opponent, friends. They're worried he'll end up on the other side in the fight.

The song says David has slain even more than Saul. The commanders quote it: "Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands…" (1 Samuel 29:5) In that tune, Saul gets thousands and David gets tens of thousands. It's a catchy song, friends, and the Philistine commanders have clearly heard it.

The answer is False. Achish tells David, "…you have been upright, and it seems right in my sight…" then adds, "But you are not good in the sight of the leaders." (1 Samuel 29:6) So he has to deliver the bad news to David's face. I bet that's not a fun talk to give, friends.

The word is enemies. David asks what Achish has found against him "…to keep me from going along to fight against the enemies of my lord the king?" (1 Samuel 29:8) He's asking to be let into the fight, friends. That's his whole question.

The two words are early and light. Achish says to "…get up early in the morning…" and to go "…as soon as it is light." (1 Samuel 29:10) It's an early start, friends. I'd be hitting snooze on that one, and I've slept in a drawer. The orders are to leave once there's light, so no lingering over breakfast.

David and his men are headed back to the land of the Philistines. They got up early "…to return to the land of the Philistines." (1 Samuel 29:11) Achish had told them to go in the morning (1 Samuel 29:10). It's the same direction the commanders asked for, friends.

The answer is True. The last line says, "And the Philistines went up to Jezreel." (1 Samuel 29:11) That's where Israel was camped by the spring (1 Samuel 29:1). So David goes one way, friends, and the Philistines go another.
